mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment (CPIAUCSL below 2% YoY) coupled with a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS below 1%) signals accommodative monetary conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of low CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between PAYEMS decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over three months signals a strengthening demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as construction and related industries benefit.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between HOUST increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS below 1%) signals accommodative monetary conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as liquidity increases and risk appetite improves.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between low FEDFUNDS and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
